text:
Anthropic built a model too strong to hand you.

Knowing a model exists isn't fluency. Knowing why you still can't touch the real one -- that's fluency.

text:
GitHub Copilot CLI just shipped custom agents. Most coverage buried it as a changelog line.

What changed: version 1.0.83 landed with named custom agents, content exclusions, and a tabbed terminal for browsing issues, pull requests and gists without leaving your session.

What it actually does: instead of re-explaining yourself every session, you name an agent and give it a standing job -- a reviewer, a tester, a release-notes writer. Content exclusions keep folders you mark off-limits out of the model's context entirely. The tabs turn the terminal into a place you can actually work from, not just prompt from.

Why builders should care: this is the exact tool running Layer8Culture's queue right now. A tighter CLI means a tighter pipeline -- for us, and for anyone shipping from the command line.

Try this this week: name one recurring task you keep re-prompting for -- a code reviewer, a caption editor, a bug triager -- and spin it up as its own custom agent. Then mark one folder you never want in context and test that it stays out.

The bigger signal: prompts are becoming named, reusable roles. That's the difference between a chat and a team.
